claims.text: For every bigrassmannian parameter tuple, the lower family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\), and no member can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
The homogeneous no-syzygy theorem used to prove lower-family minimality holds integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
The right family is the conjugate family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), and its generation was proved in the transposed version. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
For \(i=j=3,\ a=2,\ b=3,\ r=n-r=5\), both displayed ten-element families map to \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of \(J/A_+J\).
In the degreewise orders specified below, the transition from the lower basis to the right basis is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,I_2,-I_2,I_2,-1,1)\), hence is unimodular.
